conflicts.class: law conflict (R87) — the tension round 2 actually produced between R74 and the round-1 A-power rule; declared as a completed result at fix round g3 (re-measured independently, not copied from the reviewer's figures)
conflicts.condition: any wizard whose tier-0 cosmetic combo (head/cape/hat/wand) is not among the manifest's curated part tuples for its NEW live-tier power family, at any tier advance 0->1 through 0->6
conflicts.statement: R74 [LAW]: 'each combatant is the actual summoned wizard — its parts composited from its own traits.' Fix round F2 (round 1) made the rendered power family track the player's LIVE game tier, matching the 2019 reference's own behaviour (app/engine/wizardRig.js:powerForTier). Each power family lists only a curated subset of head/cape/hat/wand tuples (RIG_COMBOS), so a wizard whose exact tier-0 tuple is not curated at its new power cannot literally keep 'its own traits' at that tier — carryTraits() (N-R74/F3b, wired into the read path at fix round F3) computes the deterministic nearest match instead. R74's 'its own traits' and F2's 'power tracks the live tier' cannot both hold literally for these wizards; they can only be reconciled by a nearest-match compromise (churn) or by giving up F2's live-tracking (zero churn, but a 2019-reference mismatch).
conflicts.evidence: Independently re-measured over app/engine/wizardRig.js's deriveTraits/deriveIdentity (not copied from the reviewer's numbers): 400 synthetic ids (char-0..char-399) x 3 elements (fire/water/air) x tiers 1-6 = 7,200 tier-0-to-live-tier transitions, comparing deriveTraits(id,el,0) against deriveIdentity(id,el,tier).traits on head/cape/hat/wand only (power/comboKey excluded from the comparison, since power tracking the live tier is F2's rule, not the tension under test). Method note: a short ad-hoc script, not committed (out of this order's named scope — docs/decision-graph.* and its test only); reproducible from the pure, deterministic functions cited above by anyone re-running the same id/element/tier sweep. Result: 3,211/7,200 (44.6%) transitions change NO part; of the 3,989 that change anything, 3,970 (55.1% of the 7,200 total; 99.5% of the changed set) change EXACTLY one part, 19 (0.3% of total; 0.5% of changed) change exactly two, and NONE change three or four. Per-part change rate (of the 7,200 total): cape 0/7,200 (0.0%), head 363/7,200 (5.0%), wand 1,085/7,200 (15.1%), hat 2,560/7,200 (35.6%) — sums to 4,008 = 3,970x1 + 19x2, consistent by construction. The palette (derivePalette) is keyed only on characterId, never on tier, so it is 100% stable across every tier transition measured (0 changes / 7,200), matching §18's 'a wizard's identity is its own colours filling that shape's slots.' These figures are close to but not identical to the reviewer's cited 45.1%/54.7%/0.2%/head 5.2%/wand 13.1%/hat 36.8% — expected variance re-verifying independently rather than copying; the qualitative claims (roughly 45% no-op, the overwhelming remainder a single-part swap, never more than two parts, cape always stable, hat the most volatile part) hold in both measurements.
conflicts.law_preserving_configuration: DELIVERED (unchanged by this order): F2's live-tracking power family wins, and carryTraits' deterministic nearest-match (most tier-0 parts preserved, ties broken by the existing summon hash) is the closest available reconciliation — it already minimizes churn under the F2 constraint (only 0.3% of all transitions lose more than one part, and never more than two). The CLOSEST LAW-PRESERVING CONFIGURATION for R74 taken completely literally is different and NOT shipped: pin each wizard's power family at its tier-0 power for cosmetic purposes only (never re-deriving head/cape/hat/wand from a later power family at all), which drives the churn to exactly zero but departs from the 2019 reference's own live-tracking behaviour that F2 was built to match — trading one law's letter for another's. Recorded here as the R87 completed result, left as shipped like CONFLICT-R57-INTERNAL; revisitable under an owner ruling (no ruling requested yet — no P-node opened for it).
